profile.reading:
This OpenStreetMap point is tagged operator "NTT" with a link to Wikidata entity Q1054787, which does correctly resolve to NTT, Inc., ruling out a wrong-company tag. The location itself, however, does not check out: the coordinates (approximately 43.36 N, 5.86 W) place this point roughly 20 kilometers south and 16 kilometers west of Gijon, Asturias, Spain, inland in the Mieres/Ujo area of the Caudal river valley, not within Gijon itself. NTT's own Global Data Centers site lists exactly one Spain location, Madrid 1 (MAD1) in Las Rozas de Madrid, and no Asturias or Gijon presence appears in any NTT press release, newsroom post, or facility listing found this session. Gijon itself does host several older Telefonica telephone exchange buildings, but none of their known addresses correspond to these specific coordinates, and this registry found no basis to connect this point to any of them either.

Given the coordinate mismatch and the absence of any NTT facility in this part of Spain in the operator's own materials, this entry treats the point as a likely OSM data error, either a mistagged operator, a misplaced coordinate, or both, rather than a genuine, addressable NTT data center. No address, square footage, capacity, or opening year can be honestly asserted for a location that does not correspond to any confirmed real-world facility; this entry is deliberately left short rather than filled with unverifiable content, consistent with this registry's standard for ambiguous or erroneous source records.

reading.body:
This entry represents a data integrity failure rather than a confirmed facility: OpenStreetMap tags an NTT data center in inland Asturias, Spain, but NTT operates only one facility in Spain (Madrid), and the coordinates place this point 20 kilometers from any actual city in a river valley with no documented NTT presence.

The mismatch between the operator tag and the location is complete. The tag correctly resolves to NTT, Inc. through Wikidata, confirming the company exists and operates data centers globally. The coordinates, however, place the point in the Mieres/Ujo area south of Gijon, nowhere near NTT's infrastructure footprint. NTT's own facility listings, press releases, and newsroom materials contain no mention of any Asturias location, and no address at these coordinates corresponds to any known NTT building.

This matters because capacity data depends on knowing where infrastructure actually sits. A phantom facility in the grid cannot contribute to it. The Asturias location may reflect a misplaced coordinate, a mistagged operator, or both, but without a real address or confirmed facility, no capacity, opening date, or power draw can be assigned. This entry is intentionally incomplete rather than padded with unverifiable details.
